_about: Curated by hand from SEBI circular HO/24/13/15(2)2026-IMD-RAC4/I/5764/2026 dated 26 Feb 2026 (Categorisation and Rationalisation of MF Schemes). The daily GitHub Action does NOT edit this file; it only flags new SEBI circulars and any AMFI category label that doesn't match an 'amfi' alias below.

groups.name: Equity
groups.about: Invest mainly in company shares. Highest growth potential, biggest ups and downs. For money you won't need for 5+ years.

groups.name: Debt
groups.about: Lend money to governments, banks and companies for interest. Steadier, lower returns. For parking money and short to medium goals.

groups.name: Hybrid
groups.about: Mix shares, bonds and sometimes gold in one fund, so the ride is smoother than pure equity.

groups.name: Life Cycle
groups.about: Pick a target year. The fund starts growth-heavy and becomes safer by itself as the year approaches.

groups.name: Other
groups.about: Funds that copy an index, or funds that invest in other funds.

groups.name: Solution Oriented
groups.about: Retirement and children's funds. Closed to new investors since February 2026.

categories.name: Multi Cap Fund
categories.rule: Min 75% equity, with at least 25% each in large, mid and small cap
categories.what: Spreads money across all three company sizes in fixed minimum proportions, so it can't drift into only large caps.
stat: each in large, mid and small

categories.name: Large Cap Fund
categories.rule: Min 80% in large caps (top 100 companies by full market cap)
categories.what: Invests in India's 100 biggest listed companies. The steadiest of the equity categories, but still equity.

categories.name: Large & Mid Cap Fund
categories.rule: Min 35% large cap + min 35% mid cap
categories.what: A blend of the top 100 companies and the next 150, aiming for more growth than large caps alone.

categories.name: Mid Cap Fund
categories.rule: Min 65% in mid caps (companies ranked 101-250)
categories.what: Invests mainly in mid-sized companies: higher growth potential, deeper falls in bad years.

categories.name: Small Cap Fund
categories.rule: Min 65% in small caps (rank 251 onwards)
categories.what: Invests mainly in smaller companies. The most volatile equity category; can stay down for years.

categories.name: Flexi Cap Fund
categories.rule: Min 65% equity, any mix of large, mid and small
categories.what: The fund manager decides the size mix freely and can shift it with market conditions.

categories.name: Dividend Yield Fund
categories.rule: Min 80% in dividend-yielding stocks
categories.what: Focuses on companies that pay regular dividends. It's still equity; the dividends don't make it a fixed-income product.

categories.name: Value Fund
categories.rule: Min 80% equity following a value strategy; max 50% portfolio overlap with the AMC's Contra fund
categories.what: Buys companies that look cheap relative to their fundamentals and waits for the market to re-rate them.

categories.name: Contra Fund
categories.rule: Min 80% equity following a contrarian strategy; max 50% overlap with the AMC's Value fund
categories.what: Deliberately goes against current market sentiment, buying what's out of favour.

categories.name: Focused Fund
categories.rule: Max 30 stocks; min 80% equity
categories.what: A concentrated portfolio of 30 stocks or fewer, so each pick matters more, for better or worse.

categories.name: Sectoral Fund
categories.rule: Min 80% in one sector (e.g. banking, pharma); sectors from AMFI's half-yearly list
categories.what: Bets on a single sector. Performance depends heavily on that sector's cycle.

categories.name: Thematic Fund
categories.rule: Min 80% in one theme (e.g. consumption, ESG); max 50% overlap with other equity schemes except large cap
categories.what: Invests across sectors linked by a common theme. Broader than a sector fund, narrower than a diversified fund.

categories.name: ELSS – Tax Saver Fund
categories.rule: Min 80% equity; 3-year lock-in on every instalment
categories.what: Equity fund with a Section 80C deduction of up to Rs 1.5 lakh, available only under the old tax regime. Each SIP instalment has its own 3-year lock-in.

categories.name: Overnight Fund
categories.rule: Securities maturing in 1 day; up to 5% in G-secs/T-bills of up to 30 days for margin
categories.what: Lends money overnight, mostly to banks, against government securities. Almost no interest-rate or credit risk.

categories.name: Liquid Fund
categories.rule: Only debt and money market securities maturing within 91 days
categories.what: The standard parking place for an emergency fund or money needed soon. Redemptions usually credited next working day.

categories.name: Ultra Short Term Fund
categories.rule: Macaulay duration 3-6 months
categories.what: Slightly longer than liquid funds, for money parked for a few months.

categories.name: Ultra Short to Short Term Fund
categories.rule: Macaulay duration 6-12 months
categories.what: For money needed in 6 months to a year.
amfi: Ultra Short to Short Term Fund

categories.name: Money Market Fund
categories.rule: Money market instruments maturing within 1 year
categories.what: Holds short-term instruments such as CDs, CPs and T-bills.

categories.name: Short Term Fund
categories.rule: Macaulay duration 1-3 years
categories.what: A common choice for goals 1 to 3 years away.

categories.name: Medium Term Fund
categories.rule: Macaulay duration 3-4 years (1-4 years in an anticipated adverse situation)
categories.what: Longer duration means more sensitivity to interest-rate changes.

categories.name: Medium to Long Term Fund
categories.rule: Macaulay duration 4-7 years (1-7 years in an anticipated adverse situation)
categories.what: Gains when rates fall and loses when rates rise, more sharply than shorter funds.

categories.name: Long Term Fund
categories.rule: Macaulay duration above 7 years
categories.what: The most interest-rate-sensitive debt category.

categories.name: Dynamic Term Fund
categories.rule: Invests across durations; the manager changes duration with the rate view
categories.what: The fund manager actively lengthens or shortens duration based on where rates are expected to go.

categories.name: Corporate Bond Fund
categories.rule: Min 80% in AA+ and above rated corporate bonds
categories.what: Lends to high-rated companies.

categories.name: Credit Risk Fund
categories.rule: Min 65% in bonds rated AA and below (AA+ excluded); name can't stress returns
categories.what: Earns extra yield by lending to lower-rated companies, and accepts the default risk that comes with it.

categories.name: Banking and PSU Debt Fund
categories.rule: Min 80% in debt of banks, PSUs, public financial institutions and municipal bonds
categories.what: Lends mainly to banks and government-owned companies.

categories.name: Gilt Fund
categories.rule: Min 80% in government securities across maturities
categories.what: No credit risk, since the government is the borrower, but prices still swing with interest rates.

categories.name: 10-year Constant Maturity Gilt Fund
categories.rule: Min 80% in G-secs; Macaulay duration of 10 years
categories.what: Keeps duration pinned at 10 years, so it moves closely with the 10-year government bond.
amfi: Gilt Fund with 10 year constant duration
Gilt Fund with 10 year Constant Duration

categories.name: Floating Interest Rates Fund
categories.rule: Min 65% in floating-rate instruments (including swapped fixed-rate)
categories.what: Holds bonds whose interest resets with market rates, which cushions it when rates rise.

categories.name: Sectoral Fund (Debt)
categories.rule: Min 80% in AA+ and above rated bonds of one sector: financial services, energy, infrastructure, housing or real estate
categories.what: New in 2026. Concentrates high-rated debt in a single sector, so sector-specific stress matters more.
stat: in top-rated bonds of one sector

categories.name: Conservative Hybrid Fund
categories.rule: Equity 10-25%, debt 75-90%
categories.what: Mostly debt, with a small equity portion to add some growth.

categories.name: Balanced Hybrid Fund
categories.rule: Equity 40-60%, debt 40-60%; no arbitrage allowed. An AMC offers this OR Aggressive Hybrid
categories.what: A roughly even split between equity and debt.

categories.name: Aggressive Hybrid Fund
categories.rule: Equity 65-80%, debt 20-35%. An AMC offers this OR Balanced Hybrid
categories.what: Mostly equity with a debt cushion. Taxed as equity.

categories.name: Dynamic Asset Allocation Fund
categories.was: Dynamic Asset Allocation or Balanced Advantage
categories.rule: Equity and debt mix managed dynamically (usually model-driven)
categories.what: Popularly called Balanced Advantage. Cuts equity when markets look expensive and adds when cheap.
amfi: Dynamic Asset Allocation or Balanced Advantage
Balanced Advantage Fund/ Dynamic Asset Allocation

categories.name: Multi Asset Allocation Fund
categories.rule: Min 10% each in 3 or more asset classes; foreign securities aren't a separate class
categories.what: Typically mixes equity, debt and gold or silver in one fund.

categories.name: Arbitrage Fund
categories.rule: Min 65% in equity via arbitrage; debt only in G-secs under 1 year and G-sec repo; no InvITs
categories.what: Earns the price gap between cash and futures markets. Low risk, but taxed as equity, which can suit higher tax brackets.

categories.name: Equity Savings Fund
categories.rule: Min 65% equity (much of it hedged); net unhedged equity 15-40%; min 10% debt
categories.what: Mixes arbitrage, a little unhedged equity and debt for a smoother ride than pure equity.

categories.name: Life Cycle Fund
categories.rule: Target maturity 5-30 years in multiples of 5; glide path from equity to debt; max 6 active per AMC; exit load 3%/2%/1% in years 1/2/3
categories.horizon: Tied to the fund's target year
categories.what: New in 2026. Named by target year (e.g. Life Cycle Fund 2045). Starts equity-heavy and automatically shifts to debt as the target year approaches.

categories.name: Index Funds / ETFs
categories.rule: Min 95% in the securities of the index tracked
categories.what: Passive funds that copy an index at low cost. ETFs trade on the exchange and need a demat account; index funds are bought from the AMC like any other fund.

categories.name: Fund of Funds (Domestic & Overseas)
categories.rule: Min 95% in the underlying fund(s); 2026 sub-types: equity, debt, hybrid, commodity, overseas
categories.what: A fund that invests in other funds, e.g. to reach overseas markets or package an allocation.

categories.name: Retirement Fund
categories.rule: Lock-in of 5 years or retirement age, whichever is earlier
categories.what: Closed to new investors since February 2026. Existing investments continue until SEBI-approved mergers into similar funds.

categories.name: Children's Fund
categories.rule: Lock-in of 5 years or the child reaching majority, whichever is earlier
categories.what: Closed to new investors since February 2026. Existing investments continue until SEBI-approved mergers into similar funds.

otherTypes.group: How you can buy and sell

items.name: Open-ended fund
items.text: Buy or sell any working day at that day's NAV. Almost every fund you'll see is open-ended.

items.name: Close-ended fund
items.text: You can invest only when it launches (the NFO) and it runs for a fixed term. To exit early you must sell on the stock exchange, often below NAV.

items.name: Interval fund
items.text: Lets you buy or sell only on set dates, e.g. once a quarter.

items.name: Active fund
items.text: A fund manager chooses what to buy, aiming to beat an index. Costs more.

items.name: Passive fund
items.text: Index funds and ETFs simply copy an index like the Nifty 50. Costs much less; you get the market's return.

items.name: ETF (Exchange Traded Fund)
items.text: A passive fund you buy and sell on the stock exchange like a share. Needs a demat account.

items.name: Gold and silver ETFs
items.text: Track the price of gold or silver without you storing any metal.

items.name: Target Maturity Fund
items.text: A debt index fund that matures on a fixed date, a bit like a fixed deposit that's traded daily.

items.name: Fixed Maturity Plan (FMP)
items.text: A close-ended debt fund held to a fixed date. Returns are more predictable but not guaranteed.

items.name: ESG fund
items.text: Invests in companies screened for environmental, social and governance standards.

items.name: Smart beta fund
items.text: An index fund whose index is built on a rule other than company size, e.g. equal weights or low volatility.

items.name: Specialised Investment Fund (SIF)
items.text: A newer product between mutual funds and portfolio management, with a minimum of Rs 10 lakh. Not for beginners.
